spec.description: Fetch one item by id: a story, a comment, a poll, a poll option or a job.

id.description: Item id. One id space for every kind of item; `live.max_item` gives the largest one issued so far.

response.title: Item
response.description: One item. Which fields are present depends on `type`: a comment has `parent` and `text` and no `title`, a story has `title` and usually `url`, a poll has `parts`. Only `id` and `type` are on every item.

type.description: What kind of item this is.

text.description: The comment, story or poll text, as HTML.

title.description: Title of a story, poll or job, as HTML.

url.description: URL of a story. An empty string on a job that links to its own text.

score.description: Story score, or a poll option's vote count.

descendants.description: Total comment count, on a story or a poll.

kids.description: Ids of this item's direct comments, in the site's display order.

parent.description: Id of this comment's parent: another comment, or the story it hangs under.

poll.description: Id of the poll a poll option belongs to.

parts.description: Ids of a poll's options, in display order.

deleted.description: True when the item was deleted. A deleted item keeps its id and its place in a thread and loses everything else.

dead.description: True when the item is dead: killed by a moderator or by the spam filter.

unverified.detail: Written from the Hacker News API documentation and the live endpoint's own shape, with no recording committed yet. The Record workflow replays `examples/*.request.json` through a client generated from this spec and fills in the responses.

notes: One record with optional fields, not an `anyOf` of five variants tagged by `type`. A response union would have to be right about which fields each variant forbids, and the API documents only which are typically present; a variant that forbids a field the API does send fails validation on a real item. The request-side rule (authoring rule 0 / S12) is the opposite because a request union constrains what a caller sends, where being strict is the point.

An unknown id answers `null` with HTTP 200, which is not an object and does not validate against this schema. That is the API's own shape for "no such item"; a core turning it into a `None` or a `NotFound` is the core's decision, not the spec's.
`url` on a job item is sometimes the empty string rather than absent.
